question: Should ClawHub adopt a category-wide public-registry restriction for crypto/blockchain/finance content, or use a behavior-and-capability policy that distinguishes transaction-authorizing tools from non-transactional identity, reputation, educational, and read-only content?
rationale: Current main has enforcement mechanisms and outcome-based acceptable-use rules, but the requested category boundary determines public registry scope, enforcement consistency, and security review expectations; source inspection cannot safely choose that policy.

options.title: Adopt behavior-based categories
options.body: Publish a matrix that restricts transaction-authorizing, wallet, trading, and abusive behaviors while reviewing non-transactional content on its actual capabilities and disclosures.

options.title: Adopt a broad financial-content restriction
options.body: Exclude crypto, blockchain, finance, and trading content from the public registry, with any narrow exceptions written and reviewed explicitly.

options.title: Defer category policy
options.body: Retain the current outcome-based acceptable-use policy and reviewer discretion until maintainers have a broader content-policy proposal.

recommendation.title: Adopt behavior-based categories
recommendation.body: Publish a matrix that restricts transaction-authorizing, wallet, trading, and abusive behaviors while reviewing non-transactional content on its actual capabilities and disclosures.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the collaborator who opened and has actively clarified this moderation-policy RFC.
